Gerald Sussman and Jack Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, 2nd ed., §4.3: return-map tangle constructions for the forced oscillator

items.title: A positive Lyapunov exponent at a hyperbolic equilibrium does not produce a chaotic invariant set of the time-one map: the three-dimensional repulsive model has rate $1$ and no compact invariant set with more than one point
items.statement:
**False statement.** *Let $G:S_0\to\mathbb R^{6N}$ be the $C^1$ associated
field of a complete autonomous stability model in the sense of
[[def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-sets]], with flow
$\Phi:\mathbb R\times S_0\to S_0$. If an equilibrium has a positive real
eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $DG$ and Lyapunov exponent $\lambda$ along a
corresponding eigenvector, then the time-one map $f:=\Phi_1:S_0\to S_0$
possesses a compact invariant set with more than one point on
which its restriction is chaotic in the stated sense of
[[def-cm16-chaos-list-for-model-maps]] (continuous, topologically mixing,
dense periodic points, sensitive dependence).*
items.strategy: Counterexample by classification of compact invariant sets: the repulsive linear model has a positive exponent at its equilibrium yet every compact invariant set is a single point that fails sensitivity.
items.physical_scope: A declared-model counterexample in the one-label three-dimensional force branch, refuting the implication from a positive Lyapunov exponent at an equilibrium to a chaotic compact invariant set of the time-one map: the dimensionless repulsive model with potential U(q)=-||q||^2/2 has a complete flow, exponent 1 at its equilibrium along each unstable direction, and a nonlinearly unstable equilibrium, yet every nonempty compact invariant set of its time-one map is {0}; this singleton fails the sensitivity clause of the page's chaos list. The counterexample is a model computation; it reports no measurement.

references.title: Iain Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309, Fall 2014), Chapter 7 pp. 143-195: the warning that a positive exponent at a hyperbolic equilibrium is not a definition or proof of chaos

Gerald Sussman and Jack Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, 2nd ed., §4.3 and §7.2: the distinction between exponential divergence of nearby trajectories and chaos, with the explicit warning that a picture is not a proof

Konstantin Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Chapter 9: the qualitative chaos discussion whose equivalence claims are refuted by this model

items.title: Lyapunov stability does not imply attraction: the harmonic model is stable at its equilibrium while every nonzero datum keeps its distance and never converges
items.strategy: Counterexample on the harmonic model: the equilibrium is Lyapunov stable while every nonzero datum keeps its distance, in agreement with the no-attraction clause of the energy theorem.
items.physical_scope: A declared-model counterexample refuting the implication from Lyapunov stability to asymptotic stability for the page's mechanical models: the one-dimensional harmonic model with unit mass and unit stiffness has the equilibrium 0, which is Lyapunov stable by the strict-minimum theorem, while the datum (delta,0) has the periodic motion delta cos(t) whose distance from the equilibrium returns to delta at every period, so it never converges. The counterexample is a model computation; it reports no measurement.

references.title: Iain Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309, Fall 2014), §7.3 pp. 164-172: the corrected definitions of Lyapunov stability and asymptotic stability and the warning that centres are stable without being attracting
Konstantin Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), §3.2: equilibrium types, including the stable-without-attraction centre
David Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge), §2.1 pp. 10-13: the harmonic oscillator's periodic motions and conserved energy

items.title: A trapped one-label model: the compact energy sublevel of the radial quartic potential is invariant with finite phase volume, so the recurrence theorem applies, while the free model's energy sublevels are unbounded and the hypothesis fails
items.statement:
**Declared model data.** Take one label in the flat Cartesian presentation of
[[pthm-cm16-recurrence-for-finite-volume-models]] with $N=1$: the configuration
domain is $Q:=\mathbb R^3$, the mass is $m:=1$ so that $\mathsf M=I_3$ and
$W=Q\times\mathbb R^3$ with coordinates $(x,v)$, and the **radial quartic
potential** is
$$U(x):=\tfrac14\lVert x\rVert_2^4,$$
a $C^\infty$ datum of [[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]]
with field $G(x,v)=(v,-\lVert x\rVert_2^2x)$ and energy
$E(x,v)=\tfrac12\lVert v\rVert_2^2+\tfrac14\lVert x\rVert_2^4$. For $E_1>0$ put
$$A_{E_1}:=\{(x,v)\in W:E(x,v)\le E_1\}.$$

**Assertions to check.** (i) $A_{E_1}$ is a nonempty compact Borel subset of
$W$ with
$\lambda_6(A_{E_1})\le\bigl(2(4E_1)^{1/4}\bigr)^3\bigl(2\sqrt{2E_1}\bigr)^3=512\,E_1^{9/4}<\infty$;
(ii) the flow of the model maps $A_{E_1}$ onto itself for every real time, so
the hypotheses of [[pthm-cm16-recurrence-for-finite-volume-models]] are met
and for every Borel $E\subseteq A_{E_1}$ almost every state of $E$ returns to
$E$ infinitely often; (iii) for the flat model $U\equiv0$ the energy sublevels
are unbounded, the phase measure of $W$ is infinite, and each nonzero-velocity
free motion eventually exits every bounded set (hence visits a fixed bounded
set at only finitely many integer times), so the finite-volume hypothesis is
not automatic.
items.strategy: Declared-data realization of the recurrence hypotheses on the trapped quartic model and the failure of the finite-volume hypothesis for the free model.
items.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the page's recurrence theorem on a trapped one-label, three-dimensional Cartesian model: for the unit-mass radial quartic potential U(x)=||x||^4/4 the six-dimensional phase-space energy sublevel {E<=E1}, E1>0, is compact with finite volume bounded by 512 E1^(9/4), invariant under the flow by energy conservation and compact continuation, so the recurrence theorem gives almost-everywhere infinite returns; in contrast the free model U=0 has unbounded energy sublevels and each nonzero-velocity trajectory eventually exits every bounded set, showing the finite-volume hypothesis is not automatic. The check uses no measurement.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge), §4.2.3 pp. 92-93: recurrence, the finite-measure requirement and the warning that positivity of energy alone does not bound the accessible volume
Konstantin Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), §3.3 and Chapter 9: phase-plane energy curves and the bounded-motion discussion
Iain Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309, Fall 2014), §7.1 pp. 143-157: continuation, trapping in compact invariant sets and the limits of numerical phase portraits

items.title: Unit restoration and calibration of the two-rotor KAM statement: the scaling identities at $\mathcal I=E_0=1$, the physical angular frequencies, the exclusion of rational frequency labels, and the equal-rescaling invariance
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as in the cited two-rotor KAM theorem.

**Declared model data.** Take the two-rotor model of
[[pthm-cm16-two-rotor-kam]] with
$$\mathcal I:=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2},\qquad E_0:=1\ \mathrm J,\qquad \varepsilon\ \text{dimensionless},$$
so that $J_0=\sqrt{\mathcal I E_0}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$,
$t_0=J_0/E_0=1\ \mathrm s$ and $\omega_0=\sqrt{E_0/\mathcal I}=1\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.

**Assertions to check.** (i) The dimensions $[H_{\mathrm{phys}}]=\mathrm J$,
$[\Pi_i]=\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$, $[\mathcal I]=\mathrm{kg\,m^2}$,
$[\varepsilon]=1$ and $[\omega_0]=\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]).
(ii) With $I_i=\Pi_i/J_0$, $s=t/t_0$ the physical Hamilton equations
$\dot\theta_i=\Pi_i/\mathcal I$, $\dot\Pi_i=E_0\varepsilon\sin\theta_i\cos\theta_{3-i}$
are equivalent to $\theta_i'=I_i$,
$I_i'=\varepsilon\sin\vartheta_i\cos\vartheta_{3-i}$.
(iii) A surviving torus with dimensionless label $\nu$ carries the physical
angular frequencies $\omega_0\nu_i$, here $\nu_i\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
(iv) Every rational label in the cube $C^*$ is excluded from
$\Omega_{\alpha,\tau}$ for every $\alpha>0$ and $\tau>1$.
(v) Replacing $(\mathcal I,E_0)$ by $(\lambda\mathcal I,\lambda E_0)$ with
$\lambda>0$ leaves $\omega_0$, the dimensionless model and the smallness
condition unchanged, while rescaling $J_0$ by $\lambda$.
items.strategy: Unit restoration and label checks for the two-rotor KAM statement at declared inertia and energy scales, including exclusion of rational labels and equal-rescaling invariance.
items.physical_scope: A declared-data check of the units and labels in the page's two-rotor KAM theorem: with moment of inertia 1 kg m^2 and energy scale 1 J the scaling constants are J0=1 kg m^2 s^-1, t0=1 s and omega0=1 s^-1; the physical and dimensionless Hamilton equations correspond exactly; a surviving torus with dimensionless label nu carries physical angular frequencies omega0 nu_i; every rational label of the frequency cube is excluded from the Diophantine set; and equal rescaling of inertia and energy leaves the dimensionless model and the threshold unchanged. The constant c in the smallness condition is not numerically evaluated and no measured value is asserted.
